items.title: Tim Kelly Interview, 1979-03-26
items.q: the Melody Four that I first played with in Marshall was composed of ... Pye Davis ... and me

ctx.x: Yeah, I just wondered, because sometimes those things are kept alive. Well, it's only been, I think, in 77 that my mother would sing Scottish songs to me, which she had learned, I think, from her aunt. It was like that. People, sometimes immigrants were a little ashamed of things and were suppressed. I guess that's true. And just never did talk about them very much. Maybe they had good reason. I never did get the members of the Melody Four down pat either. Speaking of being Irish down pat. That's an unconscious…

Well, the Melody Four that I first played with in Marshall was composed of Jake Goldberg, a drummer, and Pye Atkins, James Atkins, excuse me, James Davis, Pye Davis, Piano, Tootie Buck ! Garrett, Clarinet, and me, saxophone. The first band I played with, for money, I played saxophone.
